title: Release notes + comms plan for Runtime LTS (internal + external cadence, templates, and announcement rules)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Context
We’re launching an enterprise-friendly Runtime LTS channel (initial line: runtime-1.18-lts) with monthly patches + out-of-band security fixes. Dedicated + Private customers need predictable change control and clear comms around what changed, what’s risky, and when to upgrade.

This ticket defines:
- Who gets notified (internal and customers)
- What gets announced when (RC vs GA, optional vs mandatory)
- Channels and cadence
- Templates to reduce drift across Support/CS/Sales and to keep release communications consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private

## Goals / success criteria
1) Support/CS can answer: “What changed? Do I need to upgrade? How risky is it? Where are artifacts? What’s the rollback?” in <5 minutes.
2) Sales has consistent, non-overpromising language for LTS commitments (cadence, support window, backport policy boundaries).
3) Customers receive timely, version-specific release notes and clear calls to action.
4) Minimal ad-hoc comms during patch week; exceptions are reserved for Sev1/security.

## Audiences
### Internal
- Support (ticket intake, backport requests, customer comms)
- Enterprise CS/TAM (pilot rollout + ongoing patch comms)
- Sales/AEs + SEs (deal blockers, procurement/security questions)
- Runtime Eng / Release Eng / SRE (release readiness, incident-driven backports)

### External
- LTS customers (Dedicated + Private; selective Hosted customers on pinned runtime)
- Prospects in late-stage security/procurement (deal blockers)

## Definitions
- **RC build:** candidate artifacts + draft notes; intended for pilot validation only.
- **GA patch:** published artifacts + signed checksums + final LTS release notes page.
- **Mandatory patch:** customers must upgrade within a defined window (security critical or severe correctness issue with high likelihood).
- **Optional patch:** strongly recommended for stability/perf, but no enforced timeline.

## Cadence
### Planned LTS cadence
- **Monthly patch:** target publish window = 2nd Tuesday of each month (±2 business days).
- **Out-of-band security patch:** publish ASAP after fix + verification; comms within 24 hours of publish.
- **EOL comms:** 90/60/30 day notices for LTS line end-of-support.

### Patch week comms schedule (default)
- **T-7 days (internal heads-up):** planned patch scope + any known risks; Support/CS enablement.
- **T-2 days (internal RC ready):** RC artifacts available for pilot; perf gate summary shared.
- **T-0 (publish):** external announcement + final notes; internal “what to tell customers” snippet.
- **T+2 business days (rollout status):** pilot + first wave status + any known issues discovered post-publish.

## Channels
### Internal channels
1) Slack: #eng-releases (source of truth for status), #support, #customer-success, #sales (summary only)
2) Email: “Runtime LTS Patch Advisory” distribution list (Support/CS/Sales leadership + TAMs)
3) Confluence: LTS channel page + release notes index + known issues
4) Linear: link patch release ticket + postmortem if needed

### External channels
1) Docs: LTS release notes page (canonical)
2) Email: “Runtime LTS Patch Advisory” to customer contacts (CS-owned list)
3) Console surface area (future): link to notes + “upgrade recommended/required” indicator (tracked in PM-914)
4) For security-only: Security Advisory page + direct email + optional customer portal message (for regulated accounts)

## What gets announced when (decision matrix)
### 1) New LTS line availability (e.g., runtime-1.18-lts GA)
- External: Docs announcement + 1:many email to eligible customers + AE enablement blurb
- Internal: Support playbook update + sales talk-track
- Do NOT broadly market as a feature launch; frame as enterprise stability option.

### 2) Monthly LTS patch publish (e.g., 1.18.1-lts)
- External: always (email + release notes link)
- Internal: always (Slack + email summary), with a single “customer-facing” paragraph for Support/CS/Sales.

### 3) Security patch (CVE or equivalent)
- External: always, with explicit urgency + upgrade deadline if mandatory.
- Internal: include CVE reference, affected versions, mitigations, and verification steps (checksums, SBOM if available).

### 4) Mandatory patch declaration
- Trigger: security critical OR Sev1 correctness issue with high likelihood + no safe mitigation.
- External: email subject includes “Action Required” + explicit deadline; CS to follow up with top accounts.
- Internal: Support macros updated same day; Sales/CS provided with an FAQ for procurement/security teams.

### 5) Known issue discovered post-release
- External: update known-issues page immediately; email only if severity >= Sev2 or widespread.
- Internal: always post in #eng-releases and #support, include workaround and decision on backport.

### 6) Deprecation / EOL of an LTS line
- External: 90/60/30 day notices + upgrade path; include compatibility matrix.
- Internal: Sales guidance for renewals; CS outreach plan.

## Required artifacts/links in every external announcement
- Release notes URL (canonical)
- Version + image tags + git commit SHA mapping (or release tag)
- Checksums/signature verification instructions
- Compatibility matrix pointer (GPU SKUs, driver/runtime constraints, Private installer/Helm versions)
- Upgrade + rollback guidance (Private especially)
- Known issues + mitigations

## Templates
### A) Internal heads-up (T-7)
Subject: Runtime LTS patch (planned) — <version> — heads-up + expected customer impact
Body:
- Target publish date/time (PT/UTC)
- Summary of changes (3–6 bullets)
- Risk notes (perf-sensitive areas; scheduler/kernel changes)
- Expected customer impact (Dedicated/Private/Hosted)
- Request for feedback / red flags (deadline)
- Links: RC tracking, perf baseline, runbook, known issues page

### B) Internal publish note (T-0)
Subject: Runtime LTS patch published — <version> — what to tell customers
Body:
- “One paragraph” customer blurb
- Mandatory vs optional (and why)
- Affected versions / upgrade path
- Rollback guidance (Private)
- Links: notes, artifacts, checksums, support playbook macro

### C) External monthly patch advisory (T-0)
Subject: Runtime LTS patch available: <version> (recommended)
Body:
- Summary (2–4 bullets)
- Who should upgrade (symptoms or workloads)
- Compatibility notes (if any)
- How to upgrade (Dedicated/Private pointers)
- Known issues (if any) + mitigations
- Links: release notes + checksums

### D) External security advisory
Subject: Action Required: Runtime LTS security patch <version> (affects <versions>)
Body:
- Severity, affected versions, impact statement
- Mitigation (if temporary) + explicit upgrade deadline
- Verification steps (checksums/signature)
- Support contact + what info to include

### E) Sales enablement blurb (for deal threads)
- What LTS is (stability baseline; monthly patches; security OOB)
- What LTS is not (feature parity with main; no arbitrary backports)
- Support window language + how to request backports
- Where to find release notes + artifacts

## Ownership / RACI (steady state)
- Release Eng (Connor O’Brien): release timing, publish readiness, artifact availability.
- Product Marketing (Soojin Lee): external email template + messaging consistency.
- Product (Marissa Cole): final approval on customer-visible wording (non-security).
- Support (Dev Patel): macros + intake checklist; confirms support readiness before publish.
- Enterprise CS (Rachel Kim): customer contact lists + targeted outreach for pilot/mandatory patches.
- Security (Dr. Aisha Rahman / Hanae Suzuki): security advisory wording + distribution for CVEs.

## Open questions (resolved)
1) Do we announce RC externally? → No. RC is pilot-only; external comms at publish.
2) Do we email Hosted customers? → Only if they’re explicitly on LTS/pinned runtime (CS-managed list).
3) Who decides mandatory vs optional? → Runtime Eng + SRE recommend; Release Eng + Product sign off; Security leads for CVEs.

## Deliverables
- Comms plan documented + linked from LTS launch brief
- Templates in Support playbook + shared email drafts
- Distribution lists defined (Support/CS/Sales leadership; pilot customer contacts)
- Patch-week checklist item in runbook: “Send comms per PM-913”

## Links
- Confluence: runtime LTS channel launch brief (Product-facing)
- Confluence: LTS release notes format & taxonomy
- Confluence: Support playbook for LTS
- Confluence: Runbook — cutting an LTS patch release

## Acceptance criteria
- Support leadership signs off on templates + required fields
- CS lead confirms customer contact process for monthly + mandatory patches
- AE enablement snippet reviewed by Sales (Avery Johnson) and stored for reuse
- Plan referenced from the release runbook and PRD
